data.one_liner: Provides low‑level thread synchronization primitives (Mutex, ConditionVariable, Mailbox) via dart:ffi.
data.what_it_does: The package exposes portable interfaces for native synchronization primitives such as Mutex and ConditionVariable. It also offers higher‑level constructs like Mailbox built on top of those primitives. All implementations rely on dart:ffi to call platform‑specific APIs.
use_when: You need fine‑grained thread coordination across isolates on native platforms
You require a Mutex or ConditionVariable for shared‑memory synchronization in performance‑critical code
avoid_when: Running on the web or other non‑FFI platforms
You prefer higher‑level async abstractions like Future/Stream instead of manual locking
You need a stable API; this package is marked experimental
strengths: Very low‑level, minimal overhead via native calls
Works on all major desktop and mobile platforms (android, ios, windows, macos, linux)
Provides both primitive and slightly higher‑level sync constructs
weaknesses: Experimental status means frequent breaking changes
Only works where dart:ffi is available (no web support)
Requires native build setup and understanding of synchronization concepts
data.setup_notes: Add the ffi dependency (already declared) and ensure your project is configured to build native code for the target platforms. No additional permissions are required, but you must compile for a platform that supports dart:ffi.
